about: The expert council, item 7, part 2 (queue expert-council): a personal brand system. Marketers know that a reputation is what people say about you when you are not in the room, and that it is built by being useful in public, steadily, on a few subjects, with proof. This is not self-promotion: it is making your real work findable, so that offers, clients and trust come to you. Paraphrased from common practice; content only, the screen is not built yet. Everything is optional, and a private life is a valid choice.

loop.cue: Friday, ten minutes: add this week's proof (calendar item proposed: council-brand-proof, weekly). One day a week of your choosing: share one useful thing.
loop.smallestStep: One line in the proof ledger: what I did and what changed because of it.
loop.reward: The ledger grows into a ready list for the appraisal, the CV and the next interview; inbound messages are counted as wins.
loop.environment: A draft is offered from the ledger line, so sharing starts from something true and finished, never a blank page.
loop.review: Every quarter: are the three subjects still right, and did anyone reach out because of what I shared?
loop.constraint: Consistency beats brilliance: one useful thing a week for a year outruns ten in one month.

position.say: One sentence, filled once and changed rarely.
examples: I help small clinics keep patient records safe without hiring an IT team.
I help first-time managers run meetings that end with decisions.
I help families understand their money in one page.
position.test: Would a colleague recognise you from this sentence, and would a stranger know when to call you?

subjects.say: Three subjects, no more: one you are paid for, one you are learning, one you care about.

slots.ask: What do people already come to you for?
What are you learning that few around you know?
What do you care about beyond work?

proofLedger.say: Proof is what makes a claim believable. One line a week.
proofLedger.line: When: ... | What I did: ... | What changed (a number if there is one): ... | Who can vouch: ...
kinds: a talk or a class given
proofLedger.careful: Write results in your own words. Never an employer's or client's confidential figures, names or documents.

rhythm.do: Share one useful thing on one subject: a lesson learned, a short how-to, a good question, or generous credit to someone else's work.
Leave two thoughtful replies on other people's work. Replies build more ties than posts.
One longer piece: an article, a talk, a case study from the ledger.
Refresh the profile, the photo and the CV from the ledger.

floor: The floor that still counts: one reply that helps someone. Two minutes.

assets.text: One professional profile that says the position sentence, with a clear photo and the three subjects.
A one-page CV made from the ledger: results, not duties.
A two-line spoken introduction you can say without thinking.
Three pieces of proof you can show in a minute (public or cleared to share).
Three people who would speak for you, asked in advance.

neverShare.say: What a security officer would tell you never to publish, because it is used for fraud, impersonation or pressure.
items: Your employer's or clients' confidential work, systems, tools or internal names.
Travel plans in advance, or that the home is empty.
Children's school, routine, full names or faces with a location.
Identity papers, boarding passes, tickets, badges, or anything with a barcode or number.
Your date of birth with the year, home address, or the answers banks use as security questions.
Money: salary, holdings, a windfall, a large purchase.
Anger. Wait a day (see council-6-decide.json, sleep-on-it).

measure.say: Count what comes to you, not applause.
counts: people who reached out because of something you shared
invitations to speak, write or advise
a mentor or peer who quoted your work

persona.who: A salaried specialist who never posts
persona.starts: proof ledger only, private, for the appraisal

persona.who: A person who wants a private life
